5.0.0.en: Whoever believes in the incarnate Christ and shows his faith in practice by loving others deserves to be called a child of God, since he has received the Sacrament of Baptism and lives by the new nature as a child of God, by his love for all. Whoever has become a child of God loves God his Father, and whoever loves God the Father, the Begetter, naturally loves the One begotten of Him, that is, Christ. He does not believe in Him only out of fear of Him, like the demons, but loves Him, so the proof of his sonship to God is his love for Christ.

5.1.0.en: If we love Christ, the Head of the Church, we therefore love His Body, that is, our brethren. What confirms that our love for the brethren is true spiritual love and not merely temporary human emotion is our love for God our Father, and if we love Him we keep His commandments and hold fast to them, and among the most important of these commandments is our love for others (Mt 22:39).

5.2.0.en: Our love for others is the sum of keeping God's commandments and the proof of our love for Him. Carrying out this love is not difficult, because Christ offered Himself as an example for us in loving others by laying down His life on the Cross, and by the grace of His Holy Spirit He enables us to love others, so that we have compassion even on those who wrong us and are hostile to us.

5.3.0.en: Our faith in Christ granted us sonship to Him by Baptism, and we received the new nature that overcomes the evil of the world by love for everyone, even for those who wrong us.

5.3.1.en: Do not be troubled by the wrongs of others, but ask for God's help and trust that He will support you and give you a compassionate heart toward them, so that you overcome their evil with your love, gain the salvation of your soul, and indeed draw them to Christ.

5.4.0.en: The witness of Christ, that is, His salvation offered to us, is through faith in His blood shed on the Cross, whose effect in us we receive in the Sacrament of Baptism. Christ did not come by water only, like the baptism of John the Baptist or any earlier baptisms, such as the baptizing of the proselytes of Judaism when they joined it, but He came with the water of Baptism and with His blood on the Cross. The Holy Spirit bears witness to Christ when He gives us the salvation accomplished on the Cross through the Sacraments of the Church, in Baptism and the other Sacraments, for He is the truth given to mankind in the Church.

5.4.1.en: The blood and water that came out of the side of Christ when they pierced Him on the Cross is a proof of His humanity, for He is the incarnate Son of God, and this refutes the heresies that reject the humanity of Christ which appeared in the first century, such as the heresy of the Docetists.

5.5.0.en: Those who bear witness in heaven to the salvation of Christ offered to mankind are the three hypostases, the Father, the Son (the Word) and the Holy Spirit, as they appeared at the baptism of Christ by John the Baptist, and these three hypostases are the attributes of one God. This verse is one of the clearest verses proving the Holy Trinity.

5.6.0.en: Three witnesses to the accomplishing of salvation appeared on the Cross: the human spirit united with the divinity, which Christ gave up at His death, and the blood and the water that came out of His side when they pierced Him. The three are one, that is, Christ who died for our redemption, and we receive the three who bear witness in the Sacrament of Baptism. When we are baptized the Holy Spirit takes the salvation accomplished by the blood of Christ on the Cross and sanctifies the water of Baptism, so that we are born from it with a new nature.

5.7.0.en: If we accept the witness of men, as the Law teaches us that "at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established" (Deut 19:15), then all the more should we accept the witness of God in His three hypostases at the baptism of Christ and at His death on the Cross, as we mentioned in the previous verse.

5.8.0.en: The witness in himself: the Holy Spirit working in man, who calls him to faith in Christ.

5.8.1.en: The Holy Spirit calls all people to faith in Christ, and when they believe and are baptized He dwells in them in the Sacrament of the Myron and establishes their faith. But whoever rejects the witness of God, that is, the Holy Spirit, and does not believe in Christ, describes God as a liar.

5.8.2.en: The Holy Spirit calls you to faith in God in every step of your daily life, so do not be troubled but believe God and rely on Him, and you will enjoy His blessings in your life.

5.9.0.en: The purpose of the witness of God in His three hypostases, and through the Church by the Holy Sacraments, is that we receive eternal life. We experience this eternal life partially by the work of Christ in us on earth, and it is completed in heaven by our union with Him and our enjoyment of His company. Eternal life is the salvation that we receive in Christ.

5.10.0.en: Whoever believes in Christ the Son and lives for Him receives eternal life, and whoever refuses faith and life with Christ has no place in the Kingdom of Heaven.

5.11.0.en: The purpose of this epistle is faith in Christ and abiding in Him so that we receive the eternal life prepared for us.

5.12.0.en: Our faith in Christ supports us so that we ask God for everything we want, trusting that He answers us, on condition that these requests are according to His will, that is, in agreement with our salvation and our attaining eternity.

5.13.0.en: A sin not unto death is any sin, however heinous, as long as the person is ready to repent of it, so we pray for him until he repents and receives forgiveness, salvation and eternal life. But whoever commits a sin unto death, that is, he persists in sin and refuses to repent of it, prayer will not benefit him. The Apostle did not command that we not pray for him but left it to the freedom of the one praying, according to his judgment whether there are motives driving him to persist which could be removed by prayer, or whether he is persisting in evil. In general, however, we do not know total persistence in evil until after the death of the sinner, such as suicides, for whom the Church refuses to pray, or those who denied the faith and died denying it. Therefore we continue to pray for all sinners as long as they are alive, that perhaps they will repent.

5.14.0.en: Unrighteousness: an infringement on the rights of others, as in the Greek original.

5.14.1.en: Sin: disobedience and violation of God's word.

5.14.2.en: Every wrong done to others is a weakness of love and can be turned back from through repentance, and so we are saved from eternal death.

5.15.0.en: Whoever has received the new nature in Baptism and lives as a child of God by his love for Him and for others, this love keeps him from the evils of sins, and Satan cannot make him fall into them.

5.16.0.en: We who believe in Christ, live in the Church and love everyone, enjoy our sonship to God and our communion with Him, and our conduct is different from that of the children of the world, who are subject to the devil and walk in evil.

5.17.0.en: The aim of the Incarnation of Christ is to enlighten our inner eyes by changing our nature in the Sacrament of Baptism, so that we know the truth, that is, we believe in Him and love Him and love others, and so have a share in eternal life with Him.

5.18.0.en: The Apostle reminds us of our sonship to God so that we keep our life in faith in Him and love for Him, and so keep away from idolatry, which is the various attachments of the world such as money, position and the various desires, and by this we keep away from Satan in all his forms and deceptions.

5.18.1.en: Do not forget your goal in the midst of the crowd of life's concerns, for your only goal is eternity, and your way to it is the love of Christ, by your attachment to the Church and your love for everyone.
